builds.name: Reference: Critical duel
builds.goal: Reference for Tryndamere: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A melee attack carry who builds Fury for crit chance, spins to maintain contact and uses temporary death immunity to extend a finishing window. Fix Fury crit chance and spin resets. R's death immunity has finite duration; healing and resistances must compare how many attacks land before it ends. Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
builds.summary: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Tryndamere: Fix Fury crit chance and spin resets. R's death immunity has finite duration; healing and resistances must compare how many attacks land before it ends.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Fury. Do not treat mana regeneration as Fury recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Tryndamere thrives on the thrills of combat, increasing his Attack Damage as he is more and more wounded. He can cast Bloodlust to consume his Fury and heal himself. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.

kitEvidence.formula:
Tryndamere spins through his enemies, dealing [80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2] + (0.8) × AP] physical damage and generating [2] Fury per enemy hit, increased to [5] Fury against enemy champions.

This Ability's Cooldown is reduced by [0.75] seconds when Tryndamere critically strikes, and reduced by [1.5] seconds when critically striking a champion.

Tryndamere's Attacks grant him 5 Fury or 10 Fury for a critical strike, and 10 Fury for killing a unit. After 8 seconds of being out of combat, Tryndamere loses 5 Fury every second.

Each point of Fury grants [0.5]% Critical Strike Chance.
Tryndamere becomes completely immune to death for [5] seconds, refusing to be reduced below [30 / 50 / 70] Health, and instantly gains [50 / 75 / 100] Fury.

Tryndamere hurls insults, reducing champions' Attack Damage by [(-20 / -35 / -50 / -65 / -80) × -1] for [4] seconds and Slowing by [(-0.3 / -0.35 / -0.4 / -0.45 / -0.5) × -100]% while cowering from him for [3.25] seconds.

Passive: Tryndamere thirsts for blood, gaining up to [20 / 35 / 50 / 65 / 80] Attack Damage based on his missing Health.

Active: Tryndamere consumes his Fury, restoring [30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 + (0.3) × AP] plus [0.5 / 0.95 / 1.4 / 1.85 / 2.3 + (0.012) × AP] Health per Fury (max: [30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 + (0.3) × AP + (1 × AbilityResource(4, statFormula=default)) × ((0.5 / 0.95 / 1.4 / 1.85 / 2.3 + (0.012) × AP))]).

builds.name: Fury-heal AP spin
builds.summary: Explore AP as both a physical E ratio and an emergency post-R heal.
builds.goal: Explore AP as both a physical E ratio and an emergency post-R heal.
builds.hypothesis: E deals physical damage with 0.8 AP; Q heals with 0.3 AP plus 0.012 AP per consumed Fury. Lich Bane and Nashor supply attack packets while Visage improves Q recovery. R grants a finite Fury amount and five seconds of death prevention; Q consumption trades the passive 0.5% crit chance per Fury for healing.
testPlan: Required state: Record Fury before/after Q and heal near R expiry, with actual attacks for item value.
Compare E damage and Q heal at zero versus 100 Fury, then record post-R survival.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Healing too early removes crit during R; hard control wastes the AP attack investment.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: AP scaling on E does not change its damage type from physical.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Lich Bane, Nashor's Tooth, Riftmaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Spirit Visage, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.

builds.name: Last-health bloodmail window
builds.summary: Test missing-health AD during R against the timing cost of delayed healing.
builds.goal: Test missing-health AD during R against the timing cost of delayed healing.
builds.hypothesis: Q passive grants AD with missing health; Bloodmail adds another bounded missing-health AD effect and bonus-health conversion. R prevents death for five seconds, enabling a measured low-health window; attack crits reduce E cooldown and Navori separately reduces remaining basic cooldowns on attacks. Hydra helps recover after the window.
testPlan: Required state: Record finite Fury and capped observed crit: the three crit items supply 75%, so high Fury can exceed 100% and waste crit investment. Fix R timer and actual percent missing health.
Track observed AD, crit frequency, E recycles and healing timing over one five-second R.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: CC or exit failure makes the low-health plan lethal the instant R ends.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Death prevention is not damage immunity and does not permit infinite missing-health scaling.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Overlord's Bloodmail, Infinity Edge, Navori Flickerblade, Ravenous Hydra, Lord Dominik's Regards, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
